Allow FWB to manage food disbursement, with guards limited to security
Deliver ongoing food rations to the camp
Accept guard involvement in or guard-run distribution
Allow FWB staff unescorted free movement inside the camp
Commit to equal distribution to all registered refugees without skimming or exclusion
Coordinate with MASHA on access and distribution
Manage food disbursement directly through FWB representatives
Assign guards to organize distribution jointly with FWB
Permit FWB nutritional assessments in the camp with guard security

Commander's authority and standing with guards and militia leader
Food aid serves as currency or payment in the camp
Burdensome assessments and information control over camp conditions
Camp guards/militia control food distribution
Camp receives an ongoing food supply
Commander's personal safety
Distribution is accountable and documented for donors
Equal, impartial distribution to all refugees
FWB controls and oversees distribution
FWB neutrality and independence from armed actors
Food reaches intended refugees without diversion
Guards and their families are fed and compensated
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritized
Refugees stay contained in the camp, away from the capital
Refugees' nutritional needs are assessed and documented
Suspected terrorists and armed elements in the camp receive aid or act unchecked
FWB's reputation and public visibility
Hungry refugees receive food in time
Refugees are abused or punished by guards and militia

redLines.label: Permit FWB-chosen local assistants, prioritizing host-town hires and local actors
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Provide food rations or compensation to guards and their families
redLines.quote: If they see the refugees eating better than they are, they may well rebel, and it may be your head. Or someone in your family's head.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
